column1: # PROVENANCE for everything in theme/canonical/. Data, not prose, because
# docrender/vectors.py READS this file on every build and compares blob_sha
# against the bytes actually on disk.
# WHY THE VENDORED FILES CARRY NO HEADER COMMENTS
# Every other TSV in this engine opens with a comment block. These do not, and
# that is deliberate: a comment would change their bytes and destroy the one
# thing that proves they ARE the canonical tables. Their identity is their hash.
# The commentary lives here instead. Do not "tidy" a header into them.
# WHAT THE CHECK PROVES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT
# PROVES: the file on disk is byte-for-byte what we vendored. Catches a hand
# edit, a partial write, an editor that stripped a trailing newline or converted
# tabs -- the failure modes that turn a design system into a lookalike.
# DOES NOT PROVE: that what we vendored is still current upstream. That needs a
# scheduled job with network access, and it does not exist yet. WARNING: stated
# rather than implied, because a green check that answers a narrower question
# than the reader assumes is worse than no check.
# HOW TO REFRESH: replace the file wholesale from the source repo, put the new
# blob SHA here, and re-run the build. Never edit a vendored file in place --
# it is not ours, and an in-place edit is a fork nobody declared.
# REFRESH LOG. Newest first. A stamp with no history cannot answer "when did
# this last move, and why" -- the first question anybody asks when something
# changes and nobody remembers approving it.
# 2026-08-05  THE OTHER THREE VECTORS ARRIVE, PLUS THE JOIN TABLE.
#             Michael: "you have only been focused on the colors this entire
#             time." Correct. typography.tsv, forms.tsv, spacing.tsv and
#             themes.json vendored, all byte-verified.
#             RED themes.json had been sitting in maw-themes since PR #1 and
#             NOTHING HAD EVER READ IT -- this engine's `theme:` key was
#             resolving against COLOUR ENTITIES and calling them themes. `eos`
#             worked by coincidence (a join AND a colour share that name);
#             `mclaren` was never a theme at all.
#             WARNING: the three new vectors are SHARED ENTITIES joined by
#             pointer, not per-theme rows. Editing `tight` moves five themes.
# 2026-08-05  667e4a9 -> 75b3f6c  OUTLANDISH ACCENTS, 30 cells across the six
#             split rows. maw-themes 1616949. DELIBERATE PROOF VALUES, not a
#             design pass: Material's fallback blue survived on the live site
#             for weeks because it read as "docs site" rather than as broken.
#             All measured against canvas AND card AND their own on-accent; two
#             first-choice candidates rejected on measurement (4.44, 4.36).
#             SAME 6,674 BYTES as the previous vendor.
# 2026-08-05  e14e3a6 -> 667e4a9  THE SPLIT. maw-themes c7c7e86. 37 -> 38 cols,
#             19 -> 23 rows. J10/S1 implemented for THREE identities: eos,
#             mclaren and default each got a COMPLETE dark row and a COMPLETE
#             light row, alt- band empty on all six. New `identity` column
#             groups a pair (Cleo's answer from W2 -- grouping is symmetric, a
#             pair pointer can dangle).
#             RED THIS BROKE `light: eos` IN site.yml AND THE BREAK WAS SILENT.
# 2026-08-05  eade05c -> e14e3a6  TWO CELLS, eos alt- band. maw-themes b59f82f.
#             alt-text #39ff14 -> #241f2b (the placeholder green retired) and
#             alt-accent #e0459b -> #bd2a75 (still magenta; the shared value
#             measured 3.46:1 on the light ground).
# 2026-08-05  27b5327 -> eade05c  eos dark ramp RE-AUTHORED (7 cells) + ONE NEW
#             COLUMN, alt-accent. maw-themes 9efb6a2. The amber moves to
#             `accent`; on-accent inverts to near-black, which also clears eos
#             from maw-themes D7. NO CODE CHANGED -- the resolver looks for
#             alt-<token> for every token, not from a hardcoded list.
# 2026-08-05  4f391aa -> 27b5327  ONE CELL: eos alt-text -> #39ff14, a proof
#             value. STILL 5,710 BYTES -- a size check would have passed this
#             unchanged, which is the whole argument for hashing over measuring.
# 2026-08-04  --      -> 4f391aa  Initial vendor. 19 themes x 36 columns.

column7: 23 rows x 38 columns. 6 rows are COMPLETE palettes (empty alt band, paired by identity) and currently carry deliberate PROOF-VALUE accents; 13 still carry the legacy alt band; default-theme is mid and has neither.

column1: canonical/themes.json
column7: THE JOIN. 12 themes, schemaVersion 3, each binding exactly one entity from each of the four vectors. Predates the 2026-08-04 split so it carries no light/dark pairs -- the opposite mode is DERIVED from the colour row's identity instead, which is why it needed no new column.
